newsitem.title: FINLAND: NIINISTO SAYS 96 ALCOHOL TAX MAY FALL BELOW BUDGET.
newsitem.headline: NIINISTO SAYS 96 ALCOHOL TAX MAY FALL BELOW BUDGET.

text.p: Finnish alcohol tax revenue may fall short of the budgeted slightly over seven billion markka this year due to unexpected personal imports, Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto told a news conference on Wednesday.

He also said it was yet difficult to estimate what abolishing restrictions on private alchol imports by the year 2002 as agreed with the EU will do to Finnish alcohol tax revenue, currently almost five percent of total tax income.
"Many researchers have tried to outline how an increase in imported booze affects consumption and tax revenue and there has not been a common view," he said.
"But surely when the amount of (personal imports) will rise to the maximum we will have to lower alcohol tax, maybe even radically," he said.
Finns can currently import 15 litres of beer, five litres of wine and one litre of spririts or three litres of sparkling of fortified wines from within the EU without paying extra tax.
Finland, Denmark and Sweden have been negotiating the phase-out of these limits and on Wednesday, Finland and Denmark agreed to start gradually easing restrictions from next year.
Finland's 1997 budget includes 7.1 billion in alcohol tax revenue and Niinisto said it was not possible to make any significant changes to this.
However, lifting restrictions on wine imports would not have very much fiscal impact and it may give Finland credit in talks with the EU and win time to keep taxation high on spririts, he said.
